column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:io module
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Loadable module of input/output words that were moved out of the core
# registry. They are reached only after `import`, under the `IO`
# namespace: `import "aql:io" IO.word args`. `print` is NOT here — it
# stays a core word so basic output needs no import.
# §1  stream handles — `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr` are ATOMs of the
#     StreamKind type (a closed enumeration of exactly those three, not
#     strings). StreamKind is exported by this module — `IO.StreamKind`,
#     not a global builtin.
import "aql:io" IO.stdout
import "aql:io" IO.stderr
import "aql:io" typeof IO.stdin
column3: a stream handle's type is StreamKind

column1: import "aql:io" IO.stdin is IO.StreamKind
import "aql:io" IO.stdout is IO.StreamKind
import "aql:io" IO.stderr is IO.StreamKind
import "aql:io" stdin/q is IO.StreamKind
column3: a bare `stdin` atom is admitted too

column1: import "aql:io" foo/q is IO.StreamKind
column3: an unrelated atom is NOT a StreamKind

column1: import "aql:io" "stdout" is IO.StreamKind
column3: the STRING "stdout" is not a StreamKind

column1: # §2  trace — run a list as a traced sub-program, returning its result
import "aql:io" IO.trace [1 add 2 mul 3]
# §3  negative — the words are gone from core (unbound without import)
read "x"
column3: `read` is no longer a core word

column1: folder "x"
IO.stdout
# §4  printstr / stdin — output a value without a newline; the stdin handle
import "aql:io"  IO.printstr "hi"
column3: printstr writes formatted text to output, leaving no value

column1: import "aql:io"  IO.stdin
# §5  read / write against an in-memory filesystem
#     `context get __sys get fs set mem true` switches the FileOps capability
#     to an in-memory backing, so write-then-read is deterministic here.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://b.txt" "hi"
column3: write returns the path it wrote

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.read (IO.write "mem://a.txt" "hello")
column3: read back the bytes just written

column1: # §6  writing NON-STRING data needs no options map, reading a stream that is
#     not stdin errors, and StreamKind-tagged write returns the handle — all
#     runtime behaviours exercised in lang/go/native/io_stream_test.go and
#     fileio_test.go (they return Any / raise runtime-only errors, which do
#     not belong on the static-checker spec surface).
# §8  stat — describe a path, returning a FileInfo record (name/path/type/
#     size/mode/mtime, plus target for a symlink), or `none` when absent.
#     `type` is an IO.FileType atom (file/dir/symlink/other).
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://s.txt" "hello" drop  (IO.stat "mem://s.txt").size
column3: stat reports a file's byte size

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://s.txt" "x" drop  (IO.stat "mem://s.txt").type
column3: stat's type field is a FileType atom

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://s.txt" "x" drop  (IO.stat "mem://s.txt").type is IO.FileType
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  file/q is IO.FileType
column3: a bare `file` atom is a FileType

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  "file" is IO.FileType
column3: the STRING "file" is not a FileType

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.stat "mem://ghost.txt"
column3: stat of an absent path is none

column1: # §9  list — enumerate a directory's entries (names, or records with
#     {detail:true}); {recursive:true} walks the tree. Listing a missing
#     directory or a file is an error.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://L/a.txt" "x" drop  IO.list "mem://L"
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.list "mem://nope"
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.list (IO.write "mem://f.txt" "x")
column3: listing a file (not a directory) errors

column1: # §10  remove — delete a path, returning it. {recursive:true} removes a
#      directory tree; {force:true} makes an absent removal a no-op.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://R/a.txt" "x" drop  IO.remove "mem://R/a.txt"
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.remove "mem://ghost.txt"
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.remove "mem://ghost.txt" {force:true}
column3: {force:true} makes an absent removal a no-op

column1: # §11  move — rename/move a path, returning the destination.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://m.txt" "x" drop  IO.move "mem://m.txt" "mem://m2.txt"
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.move "mem://ghost.txt" "mem://z.txt"
# §12  copy — copy a path to a destination. {recursive:true} copies a tree.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://c.txt" "hi" drop  IO.copy "mem://c.txt" "mem://c2.txt" drop  IO.read "mem://c2.txt"
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write "mem://cd/a.txt" "x" drop  IO.copy "mem://cd" "mem://cd2"
# §7  folder — create a directory, returning its Pathon. IO.folder mutates the
#     HOST filesystem via EffectiveFileOps: the in-memory-FS toggle does not
#     engage through a spec row's context layering, and `make Pathon` collapses
#     a "mem://" scheme so the scheme-routed mem backing can't catch it
#     either. There is therefore no hermetic, deterministic spec surface for
#     it, so it is the one ADR-003 hermetic exemption (see coverage_test.go)
#     and is exercised in the Go tests instead — lang/go/native/folder_test.go.
